title: Albumin–globulin interaction does not improve high-CRP prediction beyond routine protein measures in cross-cycle NHANES validation
abstract: A prospectively specified weighted logistic model test trained on 5,598 NHANES 2009–2010 adults and evaluated on 5,045 separately sampled 2015–2016 adults found no incremental high-CRP (>3 mg/L) prediction from an albumin-by-globulin product beyond demographics, BMI, WBC, albumin, globulin and their ratio. Weighted Brier changed by +0.00000435 (95% fixed-model PSU-bootstrap interval −0.00000552 to +0.00001479). Centering, weighting and squared-component sensitivities showed tiny parameterization-dependent gains, not robust superiority. Routine protein information improved prediction beyond demographic/BMI/WBC variables, but no new physiological measurement or clinical utility is established. These are cross-sectional survey-release validation and author self-checks, not an independent clinical cohort or peer review. Raw public inputs, hashes, code, predictions, unfavorable checks and clean rerun evidence are supplied.
